findings.title: `generateContext` cannot gain a required trailing parameter
findings.description: `generateContext(projectId, overrides?, additionalInstructions?, worktreeId?)` has three optional parameters at the end. Task 11 (line 220) adds "a required `adoptionStateWrites` parameter" without saying where it goes. Task 13 (line 248) calls it as `generateContext(..., 'persist')`, which means last position. A required parameter after optional ones is a TypeScript error (TS1016), so the obvious reading of the plan does not compile. Task 11 should name the position, for example second (`generateContext(projectId, adoptionStateWrites, overrides?, …)`), or use an options object. It should also update both call sites at `contextTools.ts:200` and `:264` and Task 13's call to match.

findings.title: The guide fixture claims about `test-project` are wrong; Task 12's expected outputs cannot be asserted
findings.description:
That prompt file has only these sections: `Context Initialization`, `Context Initialization Monorepo`, `Tool Usage`, `implementation`, `design`, `review`, `Task Breakdown (Phase 5)`. It has **no `context_profiles` block, no Concept prompt and no Architecture prompt**.
- Task 9T (line 194) says to add "a `brownfield-adoption: [...]` profile line". There is no block to add a line to. `ContextProfileParser.parseProfiles` (`ContextProfileParser.ts:131-150`) needs a fenced block holding `context_profiles:\n`, and `parseProfilesYaml` (`:50`) only reads indented keys. The fixture needs a whole fenced YAML block.
- Task 12 expects "concept prompt" (cases 1, 2, 5, 7, 9) and "the Phase 2 prompt" (case 10). With this fixture, `getPromptForInstruction` finds no match and `SectionBuilder.buildInstructionSection` falls back to the custom-instruction statement (`SectionBuilder.ts:109-115`). Nothing then tells the concept prompt apart from a missing prompt.
- Fix: the brownfield fixture also needs `##### Concept` and `##### Architecture` sections with marker text, plus a fenced `context_profiles` block. Task 9T's "profile but no prompt" variant also needs a defined source: a second fixture, or a step that edits the copied file.

findings.title: The parity test compares builds from two directories, but the history fact includes the absolute path
findings.description: Task 13 (line 248) builds "from identical copies" and asserts identical prompt strings. When the temp fixture is not a git repo, `readHistory` returns `unknown` with gitExec's message, which is `git rev-list … failed in ${cwd}: …`. That includes each copy's absolute path, so the two prompts always differ. CI matches are also absolute paths (`ciDetection.ts:27`) if the fixture has CI. Fix: make the fixture a committed git repo so history is `known`, keep CI out of it, or build both paths from one directory and reset `adoption.state` to `''` between the builds.

findings.title: The history `reason` brings in gitExec's network/DNS hint and command text
findings.description: Task 5 (line 118) uses the error message as `reason` and notes that gitExec's timeout message "already reads 'timed out after 5s'". But `/timed out after \d+s/` is one of the `NETWORK_ERROR_PATTERNS` (`gitExec.ts:26`). So `withNetworkErrorHint` adds a second line: "This looks like a network/DNS problem reaching the remote. …" plus the guide offline remediation. For a local `rev-list`, that text is wrong. It would appear inside the Adoption Facts history bullet and also break the one-line bullet. Task 5T's mocked error (line 128) doesn't go through this code, so it would not catch the problem. Task 5 should reduce the message to a short reason, such as the first line without the `git … failed in <cwd>:` prefix, or map a timeout to the design's "git timed out after 5s". Task 5T should test with a message shaped like gitExec's.

findings.title: Commit markers are written as checkboxes
findings.description: Lines 78, 105, 131, 148, 178, 202, 225, 251, 257 and 269 are `- [ ] **Task NC: Commit** — …`. Commit markers must be plain `**Commit**:` lines, never checkboxes. Their placement is fine: each one follows a tested task pair, and Task 11C follows the full `pnpm -r test`. Only the format needs to change.

findings.title: Renderer tests don't cover every outcome
findings.description: The Technical Requirements (slice line 336) require `renderAdoptionFacts` tests for "every outcome". Task 8T (line 174) covers brownfield, adoption-in-progress and `NOT_EVALUATED`, but not `greenfield`, `already-planned` or `adoption-closed`. Task 8 (line 168) requires an exhaustive `never` switch, so those branches exist and are currently untested. Add one `it.each` case per remaining kind that checks the outcome bullet.

findings.title: Name the module `resolvePromptFilePath` is imported from, to avoid a cycle
findings.description: Task 9 step 4 (line 187) calls `resolvePromptFilePath` without naming its module. `CoreServiceFactory.ts` re-exports it, and after Task 11 that file imports `createAdoptionResolver`. Importing it from the factory would create a cycle: `CoreServiceFactory → adoptionResolver → CoreServiceFactory`. The factory's own comment says resolvers should import from `services/promptFilePath.js`. The task should say so.

findings.title: `readAdoptionState` also reads the user-level config, so tests need isolation
findings.description: `ConfigManager.get` falls back to the user config file. Tasks 2T, 9T, 12 and 13 should set `CONTEXT_FORGE_DATA_DIR` to a temp directory, as `CoreServiceFactory.test.ts:79-80` does. Otherwise a developer's own `adoption.state` (for example after `cf config set --global`) changes results such as "No `.context-forge.toml` → `''`".

findings.title: Walkthrough step 1 may not exercise the planned check
findings.description: Task 15 (line 262) builds `/tmp/before.md` "there" in a temporary worktree of `main`. `cfl build` picks the project from the current directory, so running it inside an unregistered worktree may fail or pick up different worktree fields. Run the main-branch CLI (`node <worktree>/packages/cli/dist/index.js build`) from the repo root instead. Also, the resolver returns early unless the instruction is the concept phase. A second before/after diff with `--phase 0` would actually test "planned project unchanged".

findings.title: Partial or differently cased instructions can select the brownfield prompt without facts
findings.description: `getPromptForInstruction` lowercases the instruction and matches it as a substring. So `--it brownfield` or `--it Brownfield-Adoption` matches the brownfield prompt. Task 9 step 1 compares `instruction === BROWNFIELD_ADOPTION_INSTRUCTION` exactly, so such a build gets the prompt with no Adoption Facts, which D8 calls "impossible by construction". The guide prompt stops when the facts section is missing, so this fails safe. A case-insensitive comparison in step 1 would narrow the gap.

findings.title: A failure after the step 5 write keeps the state but never shows the notice
findings.description: If step 6 throws a raw filesystem error from `presentPaths` or `recognizeCi`, or the process is killed after `writeAdoptionState`, the state stays `in_progress` and the build returns the error stub. Later builds resume normally, and `cf config set adoption.state` can still change the state, so this can be recovered. But the state-set notice is never shown. This follows the design's step order, so it is informational only.

findings.title: No load test, and the reason given is accurate
findings.description: The tests/load rule exists only in `rules/python.md`, and the repo has no `tests/load/`. D2 explicitly says "Tests assert the caps, not timings". The bounding cap tests are Task 3T's early exit and `MAX_WALK_ENTRIES`. The Context Summary's reasoning (line 38) holds.

findings.title: The skip-pattern precedent is not in the 260 detection tests
findings.description: Context Summary line 39 says to skip permission tests "as the 260 detection tests do". `packages/core/tests/detection/*` has no `skipIf`. The pattern is at `setupCiOffer.test.ts:70` and `guideTreeDiff.test.ts:101-102`. Point the tasks there.

findings.title: Choice of file for the Task 12 integration fixtures
findings.description: `pipeline-integration.test.ts` is at `packages/core/tests/`, not under `tests/services/`. Thirteen fixture cases plus helpers would also push `CoreServiceFactory.test.ts` (now 147 lines) well past the ~300-line guideline. A dedicated file next to these would keep both readable.

findings.title: `context_build`'s error result for `AdoptionError` relies on existing generic handling
findings.description: The success criterion "`context_build` returns it as an error" holds because any thrown error becomes `errorResult`. No task tests it directly. Task 10T and Task 12 case 12 check the rejection one layer down. That is enough, given the catch already exists.
